q: What is the first law of alchemy, the one the Elric brothers repeat throughout the series?
note: Stated in the opening narration of Brotherhood and throughout the manga.

q: What did Edward and Alphonse lose trying to bring their mother back?
options: Ed lost an arm and a leg, Al lost his whole body
Ed lost his sight, Al lost his voice
Ed lost both legs, Al lost both arms
note: Ed's leg was taken first, then his arm to bind Al's soul.

q: Alphonse's soul is bound to what?
note: Bound with a blood seal.

q: What are Edward's metal prosthetic limbs called?
note: Made by Winry and Pinako Rockbell.

q: What is Edward's State Alchemist title?
note: Given by King Bradley.

q: What is Roy Mustang's State Alchemist title?
note: Iron Blood is Basque Grand.

q: How does Mustang ignite his flames?
options: By drawing a circle on the ground
note: His ignition-cloth gloves create the spark; the circle on the glove does the rest.

q: What is Mustang famously useless without?
options: A transmutation circle drawn on the ground
note: 'He's useless on rainy days.' Havoc, in the Lust fight.

q: Who is Mustang's ever-present, sharp-shooting lieutenant?
note: First Lieutenant Riza Hawkeye.

q: What do the Elric brothers spend the series searching for?
note: To restore their bodies.

q: What word absolutely must not be used to describe Edward's height?
note: 'Who are you calling a super-ultra-hyper-mega-pint-sized...'

q: Who is the Elrics' childhood friend and automail mechanic?
note: Lives in Resembool with her grandmother Pinako.

q: The artificial humans named after the seven deadly sins are called...?
note: Lust, Gluttony, Envy, Greed, Sloth, Wrath, Pride.

q: What is the name of the country the Elric brothers live in?
note: Ruled by Fuhrer King Bradley.

q: Who is the scarred Ishvalan who hunts down State Alchemists?
note: His right arm destroys.

q: Which brother wears the red coat?
note: With the Flamel cross on the back.

q: Edward can transmute without a circle because he...?
note: Anyone who has opened the Gate can clap and transmute.

q: How do the Elrics transmute without drawing a circle?
note: The clap forms the circle with their bodies.

q: Which sin does the shape-shifting homunculus represent?
note: Envy can take any form.

q: Gluttony is always...?
note: 'Can I eat him, Lust?'

q: Which muscular major loves to show off techniques passed down the Armstrong line for generations?
note: The Strong Arm Alchemist.

q: Which of Mustang's friends constantly shows everyone photos of his wife and daughter?
note: Lieutenant Colonel Hughes, with pictures of Gracia and Elicia.

q: What is the name of the Elric brothers' hometown?
note: A quiet farming village in the east.

q: What does Alphonse keep secretly hiding inside his armor?
note: A running gag.

q: Who is the Elrics' father, who left home when they were small?
note: Hohenheim of Light.

q: Who trained Edward and Alphonse in alchemy, and insists she is 'just a housewife'?
note: From the town of Dublith.

q: What title does the leader of Amestris hold?
note: Fuhrer King Bradley.

q: What is a State Alchemist also known as, because they serve the military?
note: An insult used throughout the series.

q: What symbol do State Alchemists carry as proof of their rank?
note: Ed's watch has 'Don't forget 3.Oct.11' engraved inside.

q: What is Scar's most notable physical feature?
options: An X-shaped scar across his face
White hair down to his waist
note: Hence the name.

q: What is the name of the being the Elrics meet at the Gate?
note: A white figure with a dark outline.

q: What color is Alphonse's armor?
note: With a spiked helmet.

q: Who does Edward marry at the end of the series?
note: 'Equivalent exchange: I'll give you half my life, so you give me half of yours!'

q: Which prince of Xing comes to Amestris seeking immortality?
note: With his bodyguards Lan Fan and Fu.

q: What is the name of Riza Hawkeye's dog?
note: Den is the Rockbells' dog; Alexander was the Tuckers'.

q: What is the Philosopher's Stone made from?
note: Revealed by Dr. Marcoh's research notes.

q: Shou Tucker, the Sewing-Life Alchemist, turned his daughter into a chimera. What was her name?
note: Merged with the dog Alexander.

q: Which homunculus is secretly Fuhrer King Bradley?
note: Revealed after the Greed arc.

q: Which homunculus is Selim Bradley?
note: The first and oldest homunculus, made of shadows.

q: Who is the leader of the homunculi, living beneath Central?
note: Looks like Hohenheim.

q: Where was Father originally created?
note: As the Dwarf in the Flask.

q: Who kills Maes Hughes?
note: In a phone booth, after he discovered the truth about Amestris.

q: Which homunculus does Mustang burn to death?
note: After cauterizing his own wound.

q: What is the name of Greed's chimera hideout that gets raided by King Bradley?
note: In Dublith.

q: Which Xingese prince ends up sharing a body with Greed?
note: Greed's second incarnation.

q: What is the Xingese form of alchemy called?
note: Practised by May Chang, focused on healing.

q: Who is Winry's tiny panda companion, brought over from Xing by May?
note: Actually May's pet.

q: What wasteland nation was destroyed in a civil war in which the State Alchemists were used as weapons?
note: The Ishvalan Civil War.

q: What is the name of the northern fortress commanded by Olivier Armstrong?
note: Fort Briggs, on the Drachma border.

q: Who is Mustang's smoking subordinate who ends up paralyzed after the Lust fight?
note: Second Lieutenant Havoc.

q: Scar's right arm was given to him by whom?
note: His brother's arm, tattooed with deconstruction alchemy.

q: Which former State Alchemist, the Crimson Alchemist, makes things explode?
note: Transmutation circles tattooed on both palms.

q: Where does Alphonse's real body wait while his soul is in the armor?
note: He sees it when Ed and he are swallowed by Gluttony.

q: What does Ed give up to get Al's body back?
note: He offers his own Gate as payment.

q: The nationwide transmutation circle was created by starting wars along Amestris's borders to leave...?
note: Each massacre marks a point of the circle.

q: What day does Father's plan take place on?
note: A solar eclipse.

q: Who is forced to open the Gate against his will so he can be used as a human sacrifice?
note: Pride and Wrath force him to perform human transmutation.

q: What does Mustang lose when he is pushed through the Gate?
note: Restored afterwards by Dr. Marcoh's Philosopher's Stone.

q: Which homunculus does Ed finish off by exposing its true, tiny form?
note: Envy's true form is a small lizard-like creature.

q: Who defeats Wrath, the Fuhrer, in the final battle?
note: On the roof of Central Command.

q: Which homunculus is a giant who spent decades digging the tunnel under Amestris?
note: 'What a pain.'

q: Who is the alchemist who created the Philosopher's Stones used in Ishval and later hides as a country doctor?
note: The Crystal Alchemist.

q: What is Mustang's ultimate goal?
options: To become Fuhrer and change Amestris
note: Stated to Hughes, and later to Ed.

q: Which town were the Elric brothers visiting when they exposed Father Cornello's fake miracles?
note: The start of the manga and Brotherhood.

q: What is the automail town where Winry decides to apprentice?
note: Under Garfiel.

q: What does Alphonse fear may be true about himself after Barry the Chopper taunts him?
options: That his memories are fake and he never existed
That he will never eat again
note: The Fifth Laboratory arc.

q: Who is the serial killer whose soul is bound to a suit of armor by the military?
note: He later ends up working with Mustang's team.

q: Which of Ling's bodyguards loses an arm to escape King Bradley?
note: She cuts it off herself.

q: What does Hohenheim turn out to be?
note: Containing half the souls of Xerxes.

q: Which homunculus does Scar kill by using his brother's reconstruction alchemy?
note: Scar reconstructs to use both arms in the final fight.

q: What is the name of Mustang's bespectacled, radio-savvy sergeant?
note: Master Sergeant Fuery.

q: Whose research notes are hidden as a recipe book titled 'Thousand Recipes for Dinner'?
note: Decoded by Ed, Al and Sheska in the First Branch library.

q: Who is the library clerk with a photographic memory who helps the Elrics?
note: She reproduces Marcoh's burned notes from memory.

q: What is engraved inside Ed's pocket watch?
note: The day they burned their house down.

q: Which of the Xingese characters is a tiny princess from the Chang clan?
note: Alkahestrist with a crush on Alphonse.

q: What happens to Greed at the end of the series?
options: He is absorbed by Father and dies content
He is sealed in a flask
note: Having found what he truly wanted: friends.

q: Which two soldiers from Briggs help Ed and Al in the north and later switch sides to help Mustang?
note: Captain Buccaneer and Major Miles.

q: What is the name of the flask Father was born in, and by extension his original name?
note: The Dwarf in the Flask called Homunculus.

q: How many people's souls does it take to make the Philosopher's Stone that Father uses to become a god?
note: The nationwide transmutation circle.

q: What is the name of Riza Hawkeye's father, Mustang's alchemy teacher?
note: He tattooed the secrets of Flame Alchemy on Riza's back.

q: Where are the secrets of Flame Alchemy recorded?
note: Mustang later burns part of the tattoo at her request.

q: What does Mustang do to Envy in the tunnels beneath Central?
options: Burns him repeatedly, nearly losing himself to revenge
note: Hawkeye, Scar and Ed talk him down.

q: Which country lies north of Amestris and constantly threatens Fort Briggs?
note: Aerugo is south, Creta is west.

q: What is the name of the chimera duo of a gorilla and a lion who join Ed in the north?
note: Jerso and Zampano are the toad and boar who join Al.

q: What is the name of Bradley's wife?
note: Only ever called Mrs. Bradley; she is a human who married Wrath.

q: Which Ishvalan war crime does Mustang confess to Hawkeye that he committed under orders?
note: Flashbacks in the Ishval chapters.

q: Who killed Winry's parents, doctors who treated both sides in Ishval?
note: Scar, in a moment of madness after losing his arm.

q: Which Xerxesian is Father's 'other half', made from the same blood?
note: Hohenheim was Slave Number 23 in Xerxes.

q: What is the name of the giant who guards the Fifth Laboratory alongside Barry?
note: Slicer, two brothers bound to one suit of armor.

q: Which of Ling's bodyguards sacrifices himself against Bradley on the walls of Central?
note: Fu, together with Buccaneer's final strike.

q: Where does Ed find his father waiting at the end of the story?
note: Hohenheim dies smiling at her grave.

q: What does Alphonse trade to bring Ed's right arm back during the final battle?
options: His soul, sending himself to the Gate
note: Ed then goes to get him back.

q: What is Olivier Armstrong's nickname?
note: General Armstrong.

q: Who is the corrupt former mine owner who ends up traveling with Scar and May as comic relief?
note: Exposed by Ed in Youswell.

q: What is the name of Sloth's tunnel that connects the blood crests?
options: It is never named; it is simply the circle beneath Amestris
note: Dug over decades.

q: Which symbol do the homunculi bear on their bodies?
note: A snake eating its own tail.

q: What is the name of the homunculus who replaces the first Greed after Bradley kills him?
note: Father reuses the Greed soul.

q: Which rank does Mustang hold for most of the series?
note: Colonel Mustang; promoted to Brigadier General later.

q: What is the name of Hughes's daughter?
note: Gracia is his wife.

q: What does the Flamel symbol on Ed's coat, a cross with a serpent, come from?
options: Izumi Curtis, who wears it on her chest
note: Both brothers took it from their teacher.
